paper.title: MNL-Bandits under Inventory and Limited Switches Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: MNL-bandit (dynamic assortment selection) under inventory and limited switches constraints
unmapped: Customer choice follows a Multinomial Logit (MNL) model with unknown preference vector v*; feedback is the single purchased item (or no-purchase) from the offered assortment
Revenues r(i) in [0,1] and resource consumptions a(i,k) in [0,1]; K resources with initial inventory T c(k), non-replenishable
Hard limit L on the number of assortment switches (not a switching cost)
Learner knows v*_i in [1/R, R], the switch budget L, the per-period capacities c(k), N products and K resources
Regret benchmark is T times the optimum of a fluid LP over distributions on assortments
settings.definition_quote: the retailer has a set of resources $\mathcal{K}=\{1, \ldots, K\}$ with $C(k)$ units of initial inventory for each resource $k$, where $C(k)=Tc(k)$ ... We define the number of switches during the time horizon $T$ as $\Psi_{T}= \sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbb{I}\left[S_{t} \neq S_{t+1}\right]$, and limit the number of switches to be no greater than $L$ ... Reg(T)=T*OPT(LP(v^{*}))-\sum_{t=1}^{T}r(I_{t})

symbols.Psi: R(1+NR)^2/2 * sqrt(2 + 4 log(2 T^{1/2} q (K+1) N / delta))

conditions: tau satisfies Assumption 1: for all k, tau*sqrt(log(4NK/delta)) <= T c(k)

source.label: theorem:Regbound
source.quote: Suppose $\tau$ satisfies Assumption ~\ref{Assumption:assumption}. The proposed UCB-like policy satisfies all resource constraints and incurs a regret at most Bound=(1+\frac{1}{\min _{k \in \mathcal{K}} c(k)})\Bigg(4(\sqrt{N}+1) \sqrt{1+\frac{NT}{\tau q(L,K)}}\Psi\sqrt{N^{2}T} +\Big( \frac{2N^{2} \Psi}{\sqrt{\tau}}+N+1 \Big) \sqrt{2T\log\frac{4(K+1)}{\delta}}+\tau \Bigg) with probability $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Text after the theorem: with tau = O~(T^{1/2}) and L = O(T^alpha) (q = Theta~(T^alpha)), regret is O~(T^{1-alpha/2}); this is an informal corollary, not separately recorded. The algorithm also respects at most L switches (Theorem 2). Benchmark is T*OPT(LP(v*)), an upper bound on any feasible policy's expected revenue.
